answer: In the AI Act, 'autonomy' is defined as the ability of AI systems to have "at least some degree of independence of actions from human controls and of capabilities to operate without human intervention." The critique raised about this definition is that it is insufficiently defined, as it does not specify which degree of autonomy is sufficient. This broad definition could potentially include many technologies that are not relevant to the Act and the risks it addresses, such as smart meters and scheduling tools, which may operate without human intervention but do not feature AI. To tighten the focus of the AI Act, it is suggested that models should be required to have some ability to learn or adapt to new environments, as mere independence from human control does not equate to true autonomy.
